help.title: Stress vs Strength Reliability Analysis
help.body:
Description
Stress vs Strength Reliability Analysis

Purpose
Stress vs Strength reliability analysis quantifies the statistical margin between what a component can withstand (its strength or capacity, measured across a sample of parts) and what it will actually experience in service (the stress or load, measured across a representative range of operating conditions). Because both quantities vary from part to part and vehicle to vehicle, neither is a single fixed number — they are distributions, and the reliability of the design is the probability that any given part's strength exceeds the load it encounters.

The three methods in this tool reflect the different criteria used by major automotive OEMs and industry consortia:

the German VDA Arbeitskreis method focuses on the margin between the mean capacity and the worst observed load,
USCAR (used by North American OEMs under SAE standards) compares the lower tail of the capacity distribution to the upper tail of the load distribution using a confidence-bounded reliability index,
and the Japanese OEM method (Nissan, Toyota, Honda) expresses the separation between the two distributions as a single standardised distance that must clear a fixed threshold corresponding to 99.9999% reliability.

Input data required to perform the analysis

Select your Capacity and Load variables from the source variable list on the left; both must be numeric columns in your dataset.
Choose the summary data option only if your data is summarised rather than raw — leave it blank when working with individual measurements.
Confidence level controls the width of all statistical bounds (default 0.95 = 95%)
Desired Reliability sets the minimum acceptable reliability threshold used in Pass/Fail decisions across all methods (default 0.999 = 99.9%)

Choose one or more Analysis Methods:
None computes the standard normal interference reliability and its lower confidence bound
Arbeitskreis applies the German VDA safety factor SF = mean(Capacity) / max(Load) with a proprietary four-component uncertainty bound
USCAR applies the SAE/USCAR-24 safety factor SF = (X̄ − 3s)_Cap / (X̄ + 3s)_Load using the Reiser-Guttman reliability lower bound for its d-statistic
Nissan/Toyota/Honda computes the reliability index d directly and compares it against the 99.9999% threshold.

For Arbeitskreis and USCAR the SF minimum fields accept the industry-standard hardcoded constants (1.70 and 1.50 respectively) — leave blank to have the tool compute the threshold statistically from the data. For Nissan/Toyota/Honda the d minimum field defaults to 4.76 — leave blank to use the mathematically exact value of 4.7534.

Checking Additional plots produces a normality probability plot, histogram, and I-MR chart for each selected variable, allowing you to verify the normality assumption that underlies all four methods.
